Finish the work and don't touch irrelevant regions, even if they are blank.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully added data validation list (Pass/Fail/Held) to D2:D29 via Data > Validity dialog, then saved the file.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select cell ranges, open Data Validity dialog, set list type validation, type entries, enter formulas, and save files.
metadata.explanation: Three-objective composition: (1) data validation dropdown, (2) fill D2:D29 with Pass/Fail/Held based on marks, (3) COUNTIF formula in E1 for Pass count (expected: 11). Partial credit 0.34+0.33+0.33. [Fixed: inlined _int_eq helper into check_passfail_and_count to remove nested def that triggered rule-based validator 'missing MD5 hash suffix' error]

scoring_breakdown.d_values: 0.34 - D2:D29 filled correctly based on Marks threshold >= 50
scoring_breakdown.count_formula: 0.33 - E1 (or E2) contains the correct Pass count (11)
scoring_breakdown.data_validation: 0.33 - List validation with Pass/Fail/Held applied to D2:D29

fix_history: Fix 1: Renamed nested helper function 'matches_count' to '_int_eq' inside check_passfail_and_count__9a44e82214177e638fd33343975b4139 to prevent rule-based validator from treating it as a top-level metric function missing MD5 hash suffix.

Fix 2: Inlined _int_eq helper logic directly into check_passfail_and_count__9a44e82214177e638fd33343975b4139 (replaced nested def with explicit try/except blocks) to eliminate the nested function definition that the rule-based validator was flagging as a metric missing MD5 hash suffix.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads D2:D29 cell values, E1/E2 values (with data_only=True for computed COUNTIF result), and data validation metadata from the xlsx file.
Metric checks all three sub-goals: D2:D29 correctness (0.34), E1/E2 pass count (0.33), and list data validation presence (0.33) — matching the task's three requirements.
Expected D values map correctly implements the Pass>=50/Fail<50/Held='--' logic across all 28 rows with expected pass_count=11.
Data validation check correctly parses LibreOffice list entries by handling both newline and comma separators, and verifies Pass/Fail/Held are all present.
Partial credit scoring appropriately handles cases where only some sub-goals are completed.
Minor issue: sqref substring match ('D2' in sqref_str) could give a false positive if sqref were 'D20:D29', though this is an unlikely edge case.
Minor issue: E1 check uses cached value (data_only=True) and cannot distinguish a hardcoded '11' from a COUNTIF formula, but result-based checking is acceptable here.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking sqref coverage more rigorously (e.g., verify that D2:D29 or equivalent full-range sqref is present) to avoid false positives from partial range validations.
Optionally load the workbook without data_only=True to verify E1 actually contains a formula (e.g., starts with '=COUNTIF') rather than just a numeric value.
